CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain with right foot paresthesias

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bryan reports onset of low back pain and pins and needles sensation in right foot yesterday while raking leaves in yard. Pain started approximately two hours after yard work while inside his home. He reports similar episode three years ago that resolved after one day. Pain is exacerbated with bending over and standing up from flexion. Pain improves with heat (hot shower) and sitting. He denies relief from two doses of ibuprofen. Ice was attempted without significant benefit. Denies significant physical activity prior to this event. On physical examination, pain noted with palpation around L5. Dorsiflexion intact. Pulses equal in all extremities. X-ray of low back performed and normal. No neurological deficits noted.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Right leg tingling noted. All other systems not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain episode approximately three years ago, self-resolved.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (two doses attempted for current pain)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Minimal physical activity baseline. Yard work activity unusual for patient.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Low back pain with flexion, improvement with extension. Pain to palpation at L5. Dorsiflexion intact bilaterally. Pulses equal in all extremities. Right leg paresthesias present.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: normal

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain. Plan: Rest, meloxicam prescription provided, physical therapy referral for stretching and strengthening exercises. Patient instructed to contact with message in two weeks if not improving, at which time MRI will be considered.
